problem: Normalized truncated Gaussian derivative has fractional-phase-dependent axis variance. It changes the direction of an affine signed-distance gradient, producing periodic optical normal errors without any real surface curvature.
change: Replace only the27-tap optical-normal reconstruction weights with tensor-product quadratic B-spline weights and analytic derivatives. Reuse the same sampling paths, support, ownership, fallback and anisotropic world-cell scaling. Subtract the first sampled phi from every phi before accumulation, without extra field loads, to preserve constants exactly and reduce cancellation.

invariants.result: Analytic derivatives reproduce affine gradients and gradients of quadratic fields exactly in real arithmetic. Signed-distance sphere gradients converge as curvature becomes resolved.
invariants.geometry: No contour crossings, mesh positions, indices, voxel occupancy, solver values or collision fields changed. Only stored optical normals and their visual consumers change.
invariants.boundaries: Existing sampleLow/sampleHigh clamp and fallback guards retained; weightSum and gradient degeneracy checks retained.

gpuCoverage: six production sampler branch configurations, with analytic field-sampling stubs
125 fractional phases on affine and quadratic sphere fields with anisotropic cells
